cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus, and he's been telling them to grow up together in Christ. Now he gets serious. He insists in the Lord that they must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.
Paul says their understanding is darkened, and they're alienated from the life of God. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, so believe me, dark is no way to live.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles are alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them. What is that ignorance due to?

cards.text: And it slides from there. Having lost all sense of shame, they've given themselves over to sensuality, for the practice of every kind of impurity.

cards.question: Paul says they've given themselves over to every kind of impurity. What does that leave them with?

cards.text: A craving for more. It's the snooze button, friend: in all of history, NOBODY has ever hit it just once.

cards.question: Then Paul turns to the believers. True or false: he says this way of living is not the way they came to know Christ.
Paul says the believers heard of Christ and were taught in Him. What was that teaching in keeping with?

answers.text: The truth that is in Jesus

cards.text: Then Paul spells out what they were taught, and it comes in three steps, like a recipe card. Finally, baker, a recipe I can follow!

cards.question: Step one: put off their former way of life. What does Paul call that former way of life?
True or false: Paul says the old self is being corrupted by its deceitful desires.

cards.text: So you put it OFF, like a stained old work shirt. Not "I'll patch it," not "one more season," just OFF.

cards.question: Step two: Paul says they were taught to be renewed in the spirit of their ___.

cards.text: Step three, and here's the good part: put on the new self.

cards.question: Paul says the new self is created to be like ___ in true righteousness and holiness.

cards.text: True righteousness and holiness. Friend, when God made me new, my edges came out so SHARP I'm scared to hug myself.
Now Paul gets practical, starting with the mouth. Each of them must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor.

cards.question: Why does Paul say each believer must speak truthfully to his neighbor?

answers.text: We are all members of one another
The truth always comes out in the end
Our neighbors are always watching us

cards.text: Lying to your neighbor is like your left hand lying to your right hand about who ate the last cookie. Friend, you share a STOMACH.
Next up, anger. Paul writes, "Be angry, yet do not sin."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says being angry is always a sin.
Paul puts a deadline on anger. What is it?

answers.text: Don't let the sun set on it

cards.text: Sundown, friend. Your anger has a CURFEW, and it is NOT getting the car keys.

cards.question: Paul says don't let the sun set on your anger, and do not give the ___ a foothold.

cards.text: Then Paul speaks to anyone who has been stealing. He must steal no longer, and must work, doing good with his own hands.

cards.question: Paul gives the former thief a reason to work with his own hands. What is it?

answers.text: To have something to share with the one in need
To pay back everyone he ever stole from
To earn back his good name around town

cards.text: From swiping stuff to running the coat drive. Friend, that is a CAREER change.

cards.question: Paul's back to the mouth: let no unwholesome talk come out of it. What kind of talk should come out instead?

answers.text: Only what builds up the one in need
Only what shows how much you know

cards.question: True or false: Paul says helpful talk brings grace to those who listen.
Paul says do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom they were sealed for the day of ___.

cards.text: Sealed for a day. Friend, sealing boxes for a big day is my WHOLE job, and this verse still gives me goosebumps.
Then Paul clears the counter. Bitterness, rage, anger, outcry, slander and every form of malice: get rid of ALL of it.

cards.question: Last line. Paul says be kind and tenderhearted to one another. How should they forgive each other?

answers.text: Just as in Christ God forgave them
Only after someone says sorry first
Once the trust has been earned back

cards.text: God pulled me out of a junk drawer, friend. So I am NOT starting a new drawer full of grudges.

findings.problem: The card uses facts from outside its cited verse: Paul as an apostle writing to the saints in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1) and his earlier teaching about growing up together in Christ (Ephesians 4:15-16). It cites only Ephesians 4:17 and gives no reference for those outside facts.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "What does that leave them with?" says the impurity causes the craving. Ephesians 4:19 only says they practice impurity "with a craving for more" and does not say one leads to the other.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Finally, baker, a recipe I can follow!" doesn't click. Papa Dorin is a master baker, so it is unclear why he would struggle with recipes. The line can also read as saying the earlier Scripture was hard to follow.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer "We are all members of one another" sounds like the Bible. Both wrong answers sound like modern sayings ("The truth always comes out in the end", "Our neighbors are always watching us"), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The curfew and car keys joke is a parent and teenager scenario.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line (devil, world or flesh). No earlier card gives context for reasoning to "devil", so the baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "sealed for the day of ___" asks the baker to guess the next word of the line (redemption, judgment or harvest). No story card sets up Ephesians 4:30, so the baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Sealing boxes for a big day is my WHOLE job, and this verse still gives me goosebumps" is pleasant but has no real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer "Just as in Christ God forgave them" sounds like the Bible. Both wrong answers sound modern ("Only after someone says sorry first", "Once the trust has been earned back"), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
